subject: Post-call: VanguardPay inference topology & SLOs (recap and next steps)
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Lucas Smith <lucas.smith@vanguardpay.com>, María Gómez <maria.gonzalez@vanguardpay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: VanguardPay inference topology & SLOs (recap and next steps)

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation. Below is a short recap of what we heard, the constraints you emphasized, and proposed next steps. Please flag anything I missed or that needs rewording.

Summary of pain points
- Peak traffic variability across business hours and weekends (predictable steady-state plus sudden ad-hoc billing batch spikes) — you called out ~600 concurrent requests at peak historical bursts.
- Strong data residency + encryption requirements (customer PII in prompts, retention policy 30 days, SOC2 evidence needed).
- Current stack struggles to keep p95 < 150ms for short responses (<= 256 tokens) under higher concurrency.

Goals you stated
- P95 latency target: <= 120ms for 256-token prompts for customer-facing flows.
- Sustained throughput target: ~120 qps for the inference endpoint, bursting to ~600 qps for 60-90s windows.
- End-to-end encryption and auditability (KMS + audit logs) plus a plan for SOC2 paperwork.

Model & workload notes
- Primary model family: mix of 13B dense variants for customer-facing generation and a trimmed 7B for lower-cost routing on inference-lite tasks. You mentioned wanting deterministic token budgets and structured output.
- Typical average response length today ~80 tokens; longer batch reports up to 600 tokens for internal processes (lower SLO).

Proposed topology (brief)
- Dedicated steady-state capacity (customer-reserved worker pool) colocated in us-west-2 for predictable latency.
- Private VPC deployment for data-in-transit/privacy controls and KMS integration.
- Automatic model-variant routing: 13B for minimal-latency flows, 7B for low-cost fallbacks.
- KV-prefix caching for frequent prompt prefixes, and adaptive batching windows to reduce per-token cost without violating 120ms p95 target.

Attachments
- sip-topology-diagram.pdf (attached) — initial sketch of suggested topology and routing.
- vinci-sla-draft.docx (attached) — draft SLA language + scope for SOC2 artifacts.

Immediate next steps
1) Karthik to propose a short technical runbook + a cost/latency projection matrix by Tue (Mar 23).
2) VanguardPay to provide example traffic traces for a week (anonymized) and a redacted sample prompt set (deadline: Mar 26).
3) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep dive with infra + security (propose Wed Mar 24 or Thu Mar 25).

If that aligns, I will lock in Wed 3/24 10:00 PT for the deep dive; otherwise propose an alternate.

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai
[Attachment: sip-topology-diagram.pdf (diagram, 580KB)]
[Attachment: vinci-sla-draft.docx (SLA draft, 42KB)]

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:05:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: VanguardPay inference topology & SLOs (recap and next steps)

Hi Naomi — thanks for the clear recap. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- The 600 concurrent requests figure is what we see during nightly billing reconciliation runs (short spikes, ~45–90s). Steady-state is closer to 90–140 qps.
- For SOC2, we can share our compliance packet but we'll need a joint plan for evidence collection — who will own logs and retention in the private deployment?
- Encryption: we must use our KMS in the VPC for at-rest keys; TLS for in-flight tagged by customer certificate is preferable. Can Redwood accommodate customer-managed keys in the Private deployment?

Also: Wed 3/24 10:00 PT works for María and me. Please confirm and share a calendar invite with dial-in and an agenda.

— Lucas
Lucas Smith
CTO, VanguardPay
lucas.smith@vanguardpay.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 12:30:18 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap: VanguardPay inference topology & SLOs (recap and next steps)

Hi all — brief technical note ahead of the scheduled deep dive. Added a few specifics so the engineering conversation is focused.

Operational constraints & proposal
- KMS: Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys (CMKs) via our KMS connector. Key rotation policies remain customer-controlled; audit logs are forwarded to your SIEM via a secure connector.
- Deployment: Recommend a hybrid pattern — Dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) for steady-state traffic + Private VPC workers that only accept traffic from VanguardPay CIDR. Hosted fallback in a different region to cover DR/burst overflow.
- Topology sketch (attached): single-ray router -> traffic shaper -> model pools (13B / 7B) with KV cache layer in front. We will colocate the KV cache with model workers to minimize cross-node latency.

Latency/throughput sizing assumptions (for discussion)
- Target P95 120ms at 256 tokens: with an optimized 13B int8 path and continuous batching set to 30ms window we estimate ~110–130ms p95 at 120 qps. Exact numbers depend on token distribution.
- Burst handling: use short-term autoscaler + overflow to hosted pool to handle 600qps spikes. Cold-start risk minimized by keeping warm workers in the dedicated pool for 2x expected steady-state.

Data retention & auditability
- Audit records: request/response hashes, worker id, model version, timestamp. We propose 30-day retention by default; longer retention can be configured.

Attachments referenced
- sip-topology-diagram.pdf 
- vinci-sla-draft.docx

I'll prepare a short runbook and a cost/latency projection sheet and upload before the deep dive.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[karthik_iyer@redwood.ai]
